guitar.evidence: Skid Row's guitarists used typical late-80s hard rock guitars (Les Pauls, ESPs); not iconic specific instruments.

tone.target: hot Marshall hard rock crunch with bright upper mids
tone.profile: hot Marshall hard rock crunch with bright upper mids
tone.summary: A tight, aggressive signal chain using a Boost and Distortion to drive the UK 45 amp model, paired with a classic Marshall cabinet simulation for hot, crunchy hard rock.

rig.name: Skid Row - Youth Gone Wild - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up high-gain noise and hum.
Provide extra grit and tighten the low end for palm-muted riffs.
blocks.gap: Using Boost instead of OD/Overdrive to maintain clarity while adding necessary drive.

alternatives.reason: A solid alternative for grit, but Boost is better for tight palm-mutes.

blocks.purpose: Establish the core hard rock crunch and bite.
blocks.gap: The 'Distortion' model is a general choice to emulate JCM-style saturation without specific amp modeling.

alternatives.reason: Could be used for more aggressive, mid-focused bite.

blocks.purpose: Emulate the classic Marshall Plexi/JCM-style British hard rock tone.
Provide the necessary cabinet coloration and punch for hard rock.
Enhance the upper mids and bite while controlling excessive low-end boominess.
Optional subtle thickening for solos (kept off for main riffs).
blocks.gap: Chorus is generally avoided in tight hard rock, but included as a versatile option.

blocks.purpose: Subtle echo for soloing sections without muddying the main riff tone.
blocks.gap: Delay is kept minimal and off by default to maintain aggressive focus.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet simulation with a more aggressive, high-mid focused IR to enhance the 'bright bite' required for 80s hard rock.

proposals.reason: Enhance upper mids and bite for hot hard rock crunch.
